claims.statement: The frontend is a SvelteKit 2 / Svelte 5 SSR application built with Vite and @sveltejs/adapter-node, styled with Tailwind 4 and shadcn-svelte/bits-ui primitives, and charted with lightweight-charts; it exposes two interchangeable import aliases, SvelteKit's $lib/* and the shadcn-style @/*, both mapped to src/lib.

frontend/src/hooks.server.ts guards every request: it verifies the auth_token cookie with jose jwtVerify against JWT_SECRET using HS256, accepts only tokens whose scope is 'access' (deleting the cookie for anything else, including mfa_pending tokens), redirects unauthenticated non-/auth requests 303 to /auth/login, and redirects authenticated users away from /auth/login and /auth/signup to /.

A ?clear_session=true request to /auth/login or /auth/signup deletes any surviving auth_token cookie, sets locals.user to null, and renders the page instead of redirecting, which breaks the redirect loop caused by a stale cookie.

The root load (+layout.server.ts) returns { user: locals.user, sidebar_open, collapsed_watchlist_ids, watchlist_order } — there is no watchlist_sort key. When locals.user is set it makes one getUserPreferencesService(fetch).getPreferences(token) call and copies a field across only after a shape check (typeof === 'boolean' for sidebar_open, Array.isArray for collapsed_watchlist_ids and watchlist_order), wrapped in a try/catch that swallows failures so the defaults — sidebar_open true, empty collapsed ids, null order — are returned when the preferences endpoint is unreachable.

Pages that fetch authenticated data on the server follow a uniform pattern: the load and each form action construct a client through the factory with SvelteKit's fetch and pass the raw auth_token as an explicit Authorization Bearer override, on ApiError 401 they delete the cookie and redirect 303 to /auth/login?clear_session=true, other statuses are re-thrown as SvelteKit error(status, message), and unknown failures become error(500, 'Internal Server Error'). The shell-first loads (/holdings, /watchlists, /security/[security_id]) deliberately do not follow it because they perform no authenticated request.

The /security/[security_id] server load does no fetching at all: it returns only { security_id } from the route params and throws error(400, 'Security ID is required') when the param is missing, so the shell and titlebar render instantly. The security identity and its price series are fetched after navigation by SecurityPageDataService.

Mutations use SvelteKit form actions that validate request.formData() and return fail(status, { message }) on ApiError; the shared EditableTitle component drives inline rename by posting to a named action or calling an onSave callback, using enhance from $app/forms. Login is the exception that writes the auth_token cookie directly (path '/', httpOnly, sameSite lax, secure outside dev, one-week maxAge) across its login, verify2fa, and passkeyLogin actions.

The abstract ApiClient base resolves its origin in one place — browser: VITE_API_BASE_URL or same-origin, server: VITE_INTERNAL_API_URL falling back to VITE_API_BASE_URL — strips a trailing slash, and appends /api/v1, so all client endpoints are relative to the versioned API root.

Every ApiClient request sets credentials: 'include', and an optional tokenOverride adds an Authorization Bearer header used for SSR where a server-to-server fetch does not forward the browser cookie. postFormData omits Content-Type so the multipart boundary is set by the browser, and delete returns undefined for a 204 response instead of parsing a body.

handleResponse throws ApiError for any non-ok response, and extractErrorMessage prefers the JSON detail field (FastAPI's shape), then message, then falls back to 'Request failed with status <status>'; the resulting message string is preserved so components can surface backend text directly.

Each API client module exports a factory getXxxService(customFetch?) alongside a default instance; SSR uses the factory so SvelteKit's load fetch is injected, while the default instance serves browser calls where the cookie is sent automatically.

The API layer covers separate backend areas with distinct clients: AccountClient (accounts, totals, holdings, sync, sync-status, CSV inspect/import), AccountService (cross-account holdings), AuthService (login, 2FA verify, passkey auth, signup, verify-email, logout, WS ticket), SecurityClient (/auth/2fa/* and /auth/passkeys/*), BrokerClient (/integration and /external), MarketService (search, prices, securities, watchlists with membership, sort and reorder), PortfolioClient, UserPreferencesService, IndicatorsService, AlertsService, NotesService, DocumentsService, SnapshotsService, and AIService.

The route table covers a dashboard at /, account detail at /accounts/[id], the user-wide holdings view at /holdings, broker management at /brokers, watchlist management at /watchlists, security analysis at /security/[security_id], 2FA and passkey management at /settings/security, and the /auth/login, /auth/signup (which redirects to /auth/signup/confirmation), /auth/logout, and /auth/verify-email auth routes, with /auth/verify-email's load reading the token query parameter and returning a success/error status. The loads of /holdings, /watchlists and /security/[security_id] are deliberately shell-first: they await no authenticated data and return only preference-derived keys or route identity, while /, /accounts/[id], /brokers and /settings/security await their payload in the load.

Complex state and orchestration live in ES6 classes in *.svelte.ts files using runes ($state, $derived, $derived.by) rather than in .svelte components or legacy svelte/store: AccountsListState owns accounts, selection mode, groupBy, a SvelteSet of syncing account ids, and a record of per-account sync error messages, seeding from the SSR-provided accounts.
ModalState<T> in lib/utils/modal-state.svelte.ts is a reusable rune class exposing isOpen, data, open(), close(), and reset(), shared by every create/view/delete modal in the app.

+layout.svelte instantiates layout-scoped services at component init via setBrokerService(), setSecurityService(), and setWatchlistService() (keeping the returned watchlistService in scope), which publish them with setContext under symbol keys; consumers call the matching getXxxService(), which returns the context instance, or a fresh instance when given a customFetch for SSR, or — for SecurityService only — a lazily created module-level defaultService when called outside a component hierarchy. BrokerService additionally falls back to a new instance when no context is present.

The state layer enforces hard rules: never destructure reactive primitives (it severs the Svelte 5 proxy and breaks reactivity), use $effect for side effects such as DOM listeners and load triggers rather than for computing state or fetching data (the layout starts its watchlists load from an $effect and keeps keyboard handling in a svelte:document handler), and declare a property with $state if the whole reference will be reassigned since deep-proxied objects allow in-place mutation without redeclaration.

No module-level instantiated state class or raw exported $state may be exported from a .svelte.ts file, because in an SSR environment that bleeds one user's state into another user's request; the instance must be created in a component or layout and passed down through context.

Multi-step fetches are orchestrated inside a single service method rather than sequenced in a component: AccountsListState.syncAccount posts the sync request and then polls getSyncStatus until the account leaves the in-flight list, and WatchlistService.addSecurity short-circuits when the target list already holds the same symbol + exchange (the backend does not dedupe membership), reuses a security id already present in any watchlist before falling back to createOrUpdateSecurity, and only then posts the membership request.

Services store real error message strings rather than a generic boolean error flag — BrokerService, WatchlistService, and SecurityService each expose an error string, and AccountsListState keeps a per-account syncErrors record — so the UI layer can render actionable feedback; all API calls in frontend tests must be mocked, since CI runs without a backend and an unmocked fetch fails the suite.

AccountsListState opens a WebSocket to /api/ws (URL derived from an absolute VITE_API_BASE_URL when present, otherwise from window.location) using a short-lived signed ticket from authService.getWsTicket(), maintains syncingAccountIds and syncErrors from the sync_started, sync_finished, and sync_failed event types, hydrates in-flight syncs from the sync-status endpoint on open, and reconnects on a 5-second timer after close.

syncAccount guards against lost pub/sub messages by polling the sync-status endpoint in waitForSyncFinish with a 60-second deadline, a 1.5-second interval, and a 5-second grace period after the account leaves the in-flight list, clearing the sync state and refetching accounts or setting a timeout error message.

The authenticated shell in +layout.svelte composes Sidebar.Provider bound to a sidebarOpen state seeded from data.sidebar_open inside untrack, with AppSidebar and Sidebar.Inset wrapping page content; it instantiates the layout-scoped services, runs a single $effect that awaits watchlistService.loadWatchlists() once data.user is set and routes a non-null error through redirectOn401, warms the shortcut targets with preloadData (each URL at most once via a per-instance SvelteSet, failures swallowed), persists sidebar changes through userPreferencesService.patchPreferences({ sidebar_open: open }), owns globalSearchOpen plus globalSearchTargetWatchlist, publishes them via setContext('toggleGlobalSearch') and setContext('openGlobalSearch'), and renders GlobalSearch with bind:open and bind:targetWatchlist.

AppSidebar is collapsible to icon size and stacks AppSidebarHeader (brand link to / plus the sidebar trigger), AppSidebarActions (a Search entry invoking the toggleGlobalSearch context callback with a / hint, a Watchlists link to /watchlists with a w hint, and a Holdings link to /holdings with an h hint, both links built with resolve from $app/paths), AppSidebarWatchlist (renders every watchlist from getWatchlistService().watchlists as a collapsible group, not just the default one), and AppSidebarProfile (footer dropdown with the user email and navigation to /brokers, /settings/security, and a native POST form to /auth/logout).

GlobalSearch is a Command.Dialog bound to the layout's open state and to a $bindable targetWatchlist; it debounces marketService.search by 300 ms, groups results by security_type, and on select calls createOrUpdateSecurity then goto('/security/{id}'). Its star button is target-aware: it resolves the bound target against the service's current watchlists, matches a result by symbol plus exchange, and either removes/adds membership on that target list or — with no target — falls back to defaultWatchlistSecurities and delegates to toggleSecurity, so an existing security is toggled rather than re-created. Closing the dialog resets the query, the results, and the bound target.

Type and money conventions: backend fields are mirrored as snake_case, list endpoints return PaginatedResponse<T> with an items array, and Money is { value?, units?, nanos?, currencyCode? } where moneyToNumber prefers units plus nanos/1e9 and falls back to parsing the string value while money() renders a localized dollar amount. Account holdings totals are nested as { cost: Money, value: Money }.

Account and institution domain enums live in lib/types/account.ts with getAccountTypeLabel and getInstitutionLabel helpers that accept an optional translate callback, and AccountHoldings extends PaginatedResponse<Holding> with account-level totals (total_value, total_profit_loss, total_profit_loss_percent, net_deposits, currency) consumed by the account detail header and the account-scoped holdings table.

Frontend tests use Vitest with jsdom and @testing-library/svelte configured in vite.config.ts (environment jsdom, url http://localhost/, setupFiles ./src/setupTest.ts, include src/**/*.test|spec), with setupTest.ts registering jest-dom, stubbing window.location, and deferring teardown ~50 ms so bits-ui body-scroll-lock timers do not throw after jsdom is destroyed; tests must mock every API client module and stub each method the component calls, and must also mock framework or third-party modules that reach the network or DOM ($app/forms, $app/paths, $app/navigation, $app/stores, lightweight-charts), replacing global.WebSocket in websocket tests.

hooks.server.test.ts runs under the node vitest environment, mocks $env/static/private, signs real HS256 tokens with jose for each case, and covers token-scope rejection such as mfa_pending tokens clearing the cookie while leaving locals.user null.

The frontend extension points are consistent: a new backend area is a class extending ApiClient exported as both a getXClient factory and a default instance; a new page either uses the standard load shape (401-delete-and-redirect / ApiError-to-error) when its payload must be awaited, or returns only cheap route-identity/preference keys and gives the page a *.svelte.ts service whose load() returns the caught error for redirectOn401; a new stateful feature is a Foo.svelte.ts rune class with isLoading and message-valued error state instantiated in the component that owns the state (as /holdings does with HoldingsService and the security route with SecurityPageDataService) or provided from +layout.svelte; and a new preference is a field added to UserPreferences in userPreferencesService.ts, patched from the component with patchPreferences, where shell-driving preferences are additionally read in +layout.server.ts's load behind a shape check inside the existing try/catch while page-scoped ones like holdings_table and holdings_group are read in that page's own +page.server.ts load inside a nested try/catch.

The /watchlists server load performs no fetching and no auth handling: it is a synchronous load returning { watchlists: [] }, and the tests assert that neither the market client nor event.fetch is called and that the auth_token cookie is never read or deleted. The empty array exists only to keep the page's seeding guard prop shape intact; the watchlists themselves come from the layout-owned WatchlistService.

The /watchlists page renders one section per watchlist with security links to /security/{id}, formatted price and daily-change pills, inline rename, a confirmation-modal delete, per-watchlist sort selection, a watchlist Reorder mode with drag-and-drop, and a per-list security reorder mode offered only while that list's sort is custom. It reads the shared WatchlistService instance from context (seeding watchlistService.watchlists from its SSR data only when the service is still empty), keeps its own watchlistOrder $state seeded from data or $page.data, and persists reorders as patchPreferences({ watchlist_order }) with both local snapshots restored on failure, while sort choices go through WatchlistService.setSort (PATCH /market/watchlists/{id}) rather than a preference. Its per-watchlist '+' button calls the layout's openGlobalSearch context callback with that watchlist.

WatchlistService is the single client-side owner of watchlist data: its constructor only wires getMarketService(customFetch), loadWatchlists(token) stores the array returned by GET /market/watchlists directly (each watchlist already carries its embedded securities, so there is no resolve-then-fetch step) and returns the caught error, defaultWatchlistSecurities is a $derived lookup for name === 'Default' that backs hasSecurity and toggleSecurity (and therefore the id-less addToWatchlist/removeFromWatchlist shortcuts), and every write returning a WatchlistRead goes through replaceWatchlist(updated) which swaps one element by id while createWatchlist appends and deleteWatchlist filters. reorderSecurities applies its new order optimistically (positions rewritten to index) before the PUT resolves and setSort applies none because the response is already ordered; removeSecurityFromWatchlist, reorderSecurities and toggleSecurity re-run loadWatchlists in their catch to resynchronise after a failed write, whereas removeSecurity only records the error message.

Layout-level preferences are server-loaded and client-persisted in one round trip: sidebar_open, collapsed_watchlist_ids and watchlist_order are read in +layout.server.ts and written back with userPreferencesService.patchPreferences from the component owning the interaction (the layout's sidebar handler, AppSidebarWatchlist.toggleCollapsed, and the /watchlists reorder handler), always as fire-and-forget calls that only log on failure — except the /watchlists reorder, which reverts its optimistic state and surfaces the message. Page-scoped holdings preferences follow the same write path but are read by the /holdings load: holdings_table and holdings_group feed holdings_table_config and group_mode, are patched through saveHoldingsTableConfig / saveHoldingsGroupMode, and their rejections are surfaced in a page-level persistError instead of only being logged. Per-watchlist security sort is not a preference at all — it lives on WatchlistRead.sort and is persisted through WatchlistService.setSort. sidebar_watchlists is declared on UserPreferences but is not read by any component or load.

Watchlist ordering and collapse state are presentation layers over the shared service data: sortWatchlistsByOrder(watchlists, order) in watchlist-utils.ts sorts by index in the persisted id array and appends watchlists absent from it in their original relative order, and sortSecurities(securities, sortKey) implements custom (ascending position), name_asc, name_desc, price_change_desc, price_change_asc, date_added and date_added_asc, falling back to custom order for an absent or unrecognised key, with normalizeWatchlistSort narrowing a persisted key to that union. AppSidebarWatchlist resolves watchlist_order and collapsed_watchlist_ids from a setContext seam first (used by app-sidebar.test-harness.svelte), then from $page.data, keeps collapse state in a SvelteSet, and persists the whole set on toggle; the /watchlists page applies the same two helpers to the same service data.

MarketService covers both watchlist membership styles plus the paginated per-list read and manual reordering: the id-less default-list shortcuts POST/DELETE /market/watchlists/securities/{securityId} (backed by addToWatchlist/removeFromWatchlist), the per-list POST/DELETE /market/watchlists/{watchlistId}/securities/{securityId} (addSecurityToWatchlist/removeSecurityFromWatchlist), GET /market/watchlists/{watchlistId}/securities returning PaginatedResponse of SecuritySchema, and PUT /market/watchlists/{watchlistId}/securities/order with { security_ids } (reorderWatchlistSecurities, which requires an exact permutation of the current membership), alongside watchlist list/create/rename/delete and updateWatchlistSort (the same PATCH /market/watchlists/{id} carrying { sort }).

setupTest.ts additionally no-ops Element.prototype.scrollIntoView because bits-ui's Command calls it asynchronously on the active item and closest group heading, and suppresses only the DEV-only derived_inert console warning emitted by bits-ui's dismissible-layer afterSleep timers while forwarding every other warning.

Route-level tests exercise the shell and page components directly with mocked clients instead of a running server: routes/layout.test.ts renders +layout.svelte with a createRawSnippet child to assert the unauthenticated bare-children path versus the Sidebar.Provider path, drives the keyboard shortcuts and their typing/modifier guards, asserts the prefetch order and one-shot behavior, and calls the +layout.server.ts load with a fake event to check collapsed_watchlist_ids and watchlist_order defaults; routes/watchlists/page.svelte.test.ts mocks the market client and preferences service while keeping a real WatchlistService instance (mocking only getWatchlistService) so the page's $derived ordering and sorting run against real rune state; routes/security/[security_id]/page.server.test.ts asserts the load returns only security_id; and the colocated /holdings suites mock $lib/api/accountService and $lib/api/userPreferencesService (plus $app/paths and $app/navigation in the component test) to drive the load, the post-navigation paging, and the page's grouping, column visibility and per-currency totals without any backend.

The /holdings server load awaits no holdings rows and has no form actions: it starts from normalized defaults and, inside a non-fatal nested try/catch, makes one getUserPreferencesService(fetch).getPreferences(token) call that normalizes holdings_table and holdings_group and forwards elliott_waves, returning { holdings_table_config, group_mode, elliott_waves }. The rows are fetched after navigation by the page's own HoldingsService. Its tests assert the returned key set and that getUserHoldings is never called, and that a preferences rejection falls back to the default table config, flat grouping and null Elliott waves.

AccountService covers both holdings scopes: getHoldings(securityId) reads the per-security account breakdown at /accounts/holdings/{securityId}, and getUserHoldings(offset = 0, limit = 50, token?) reads the user-wide paginated GET /accounts/holdings?offset=&limit= typed as PaginatedResponse<UserHolding>, passing the same optional SSR token override that factory-built clients use.

The /holdings page instantiates its own HoldingsService at component init, seeds only the group mode from the server data (service.setGroupBy(data.group_mode)) so toggling grouping re-renders from memory instead of refetching, and fetches the rows from an $effect that awaits service.load() and routes a non-null error through redirectOn401; groupBy is a rune and groupedHoldings is a $derived.by over groupHoldings(rows, mode) from lib/utils/finance/holdings-group.ts. The same module exports setHoldingsService() / getHoldingsService(customFetch?) under Symbol('holdings-service'), where the customFetch call returns an isolated instance, but no production component reads that context.

HoldingsService.load(token) is the post-navigation data wave for /holdings: it pages getUserHoldings with PAGE_SIZE 50 until offset >= total or an empty page, capped at MAX_PAGES 100 as a stale-total safety valve, accumulates every page before assigning rows, keeps the previous rows when a page rejects, stores the thrown message (Error message or String(error)) in errorMessage, and returns the caught error (or null on success) so the caller can route a 401 through the shared async-data seam — which is exactly what the /holdings page's mount effect does.

UserHolding in lib/types/account.ts is Holding extended with account_id and account_name, mirroring the backend UserHoldingRead returned by the user-wide GET /accounts/holdings; it is the row type of the /holdings table (rows arrive via HoldingsService, typed UserHolding[]), which is what lets that view render an Account column and aggregate one stock across accounts.

UserPreferences in lib/api/userPreferencesService.ts carries the holdings preferences holdings_table (HoldingsTableConfig from components/holdings/holdings-table-columns) and holdings_group (HoldingsGroupMode from lib/utils/finance/holdings-group) alongside the sidebar, watchlist, holdings_period, chart (timeframe, chart_style, indicators, chart_hide_labels, indicator_pane_heights) and drawing (elliott_waves, fibonacci_tools, drawings, wave_settings) fields, and the same module re-exports the Elliott-wave, Fibonacci and drawing persistence shapes that are declared under $lib/utils/finance/.

Holdings are rendered by two independent, route-scoped tables with no shared component between them: /accounts/[id] feeds the older components/accounts/holdings-table.svelte from an AccountHoldings payload awaited in its server load, while /holdings feeds components/holdings/holdings-table.svelte from the page-owned HoldingsService rows plus tableConfig, groupBy, elliottWaves and an onConfigChange callback that the page uses to persist column changes.

The post-navigation data wave is a shared frontend convention: a route's +page.server.ts returns only cheap route identity or preference-derived keys, a page-owned *.svelte.ts service performs the real fetch from an $effect (which never runs during SSR), and the service's load() never throws — it stores the message in its own error state and returns the caught error, or null on success. The calling effect passes a non-null result to redirectOn401 from $lib/api/async-data.ts, which returns true only for an ApiError with status 401, navigates to /auth/login?clear_session=true and leaves the httpOnly cookie to be cleared by hooks.server.ts, and returns false otherwise so the caller surfaces err.message in its own in-page alert.

SecurityPageDataService (routes/security/[security_id]/page-data.svelte.ts) owns the security route's post-navigation wave: load(securityId) fetches the security identity and its price series in parallel with Promise.all inside getChartDateWindow(new SvelteDate(), '1d'), bumps a private loadSeq and discards its own result when a newer soft navigation has started (so a slow response cannot clobber the current security), and treats a missing or empty series as a successful load whose message ('No price data available for this security') lands in error rather than being thrown. The page renders the titlebar from the already-loaded default watchlist while the fetch is in flight.

The layout's document-level keyboard handler provides modifier-free shortcuts: it returns early when meta/ctrl/alt is held or the event target is an INPUT, TEXTAREA, SELECT or contenteditable element, then binds / to toggle global search, w to /watchlists, h to /holdings, and 1-9/0 to the first nine/tenth security of the default watchlist (prefetching the target before navigating).

Once the layout's watchlists load resolves, the same effect warms the shortcut targets with preloadData(resolve(url)): /watchlists, /holdings, and up to ten securities from watchlistService.defaultWatchlistSecurities.slice(0, 10), in that order. Prefetches are fire-and-forget (nothing render-related awaits them), each URL is warmed at most once through a per-instance SvelteSet rather than module scope, and a rejected prefetch is swallowed because the real navigation load still runs.

Per-watchlist security sort is stored on the watchlist row, not in user preferences: WatchlistRead.sort is a WatchlistSort union ('custom', 'name_asc', 'price_change_desc', 'price_change_asc', 'date_added', 'date_added_asc') and is persisted through WatchlistService.setSort -> PATCH /market/watchlists/{watchlistId} with { sort }, whose response already carries the securities ordered by the backend. No frontend code reads or writes a watchlist_sort preference key.
